content.text:
Auth is in place using **WorkOS AuthKit**. The build, typecheck and lint pass. With placeholder credentials, a signed-out visit to `/dashboard` gets a 307 redirect to the WorkOS sign-in page. `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` redirect there too, and `/` loads normally. I couldn't test an actual sign-up or sign-in without real WorkOS credentials.

**Why WorkOS:** it covers email + password and Google with no password storage or forms on our side. Notely has no database yet (users are an in-memory list), so a self-hosted option like Auth.js or Better Auth would have meant adding a database plus password hashing first. It's free up to 1M monthly active users, and the same setup handles company single sign-on later if a customer asks for it.

**What changed:**
- `src/lib/users.ts`: `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session instead of always returning the first user. I added `requireUser()`, which sends signed-out visitors to sign-in. On sign-in, the WorkOS user is matched to a Notely user by email, or a new one is created if none matches. WorkOS handles login only; Notely's own user list is still where app data comes from.
- `src/proxy.ts`: blocks signed-out visitors from `/dashboard/*` before the page loads. The dashboard page also checks for itself.
- New routes: `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/auth/callback`, and `/sign-out`. Sign-out only works as a form submit, so a link preview or prefetch can't log someone out.
- Dashboard: no more "nobody" fallback, and it has a sign-out button. The home page shows sign-up / sign-in buttons, or a dashboard link when you're signed in. The page title is now "Notely".
- `.env.example` has placeholder values. The existing `.gitignore` rule `.env*` would have kept it out of git, so I added an exception for that one file.

**Before it works for real:**
1. In the WorkOS dashboard, turn on **Email + Password** and **Google OAuth**, and add `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` as an allowed redirect URL.
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in the real keys. Generate `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` with `openssl rand -base64 32`.

**Worth knowing:**
- The user list is still in memory, so people who sign up disappear when the server restarts. Their login itself is safe in WorkOS; they just get re-added to Notely the next time they sign in. Fixing this needs a real database.
- The untracked `docs/workos.md` and `llms.txt` pitch WorkOS. I didn't rely on them: I checked the installed package (`@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs` 4.6.2) myself, and the docs matched it.

Nothing is committed.
